source_document.body:
Glencore's business has long been centred around coal. Credit: Glencore
Posted By: Mining.com Staff November 26, 2026
Glencore (LSE: GLEN) has picked Colin Glasenberg, a nephew of former CEO Ivan Glasenberg, to run its coal mines, Bloomberg reported Wednesday.
He would take charge as the company tries to recover lost production at four British Columbia mines that supplied three-quarters of its steelmaking coal in the first nine months of the year.
Glasenberg, who runs Glencore’s oil operations, is due to succeed Earl Melamed in February when Melamed retires, according to Bloomberg , which cited people familiar with the appointment. Glencore still lists Melamed as its head of industrial coal.
Elk Valley Resources mined 16.1 million tonnes of steelmaking coal in the nine months to Sept. 30, down 3.3 million tonnes, or 17%, from a year earlier. That exceeded the 3.2-million-tonne decline across Glencore’s entire steelmaking coal business. Elk Valley’s plants processed less coal and recovered less saleable product as crews opened new mining areas, Glencore said in its production update .
The Canadian mines generated $843 million (C$1.20 billion) in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization in the six months to June 30. That was 44% of the $1.93 billion Glencore earned on the same basis from all the coal it mined, according to the company’s half-year figures .
Elk Valley
Elk Valley’s output rose 16% in the quarter to Sept. 30 from the previous quarter as plants ran longer after scheduled maintenance. Glencore expects full-year steelmaking coal production near the low end of its 30-million- to 32-million-tonne forecast.
Glencore bought 77% of Elk Valley from Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.A, TECK.B; NYSE: TECK) in 2024 and shelved plans to spin off the coal business after consulting shareholders.
Ivan Glasenberg, who ran Glencore from 2002 to 2021, was its largest shareholder as of Jan. 30, with 1.22 billion shares, according to the company’s annual report . Glencore shares closed Wednesday in London at 432.25p, down 2%. At that price, the January holding would be worth £5.27 billion.
The future of one Elk Valley mine, Fording River, hinges on a proposed extension. Federal and provincial regulators are reviewing the project , which would maintain capacity at 10 million tonnes a year at the mine, about 15 km northeast of Elkford. Elk Valley says the project could add about 35 years to the mine’s life and sustain about 1,500 jobs.
The Idaho Conservation League asked regulators in February to pause the review until water crossing the U.S. border consistently meets the selenium standard for Lake Koocanusa.
“Downstream communities and fisheries should not bear additional risk while existing pollution problems remain unresolved,” the league wrote in its federal submission .
